principle_text: When the seller immediately accepts a lower price offer and adds extra benefits, you should leverage any available price references to negotiate a better deal.
When the seller justifies the price by offering additional items, avoid proposing to pick up the item yourself to reduce costs, as it may not lead to a lower price.
When the seller is firm on the price and has already included additional items, avoid accepting the offer without further negotiation to prevent conceding to a higher price than desired.
When the seller confirms the item is unused and in excellent condition, you should emphasize the item's like-new quality to justify a higher asking price.
When the seller explains the reason for not using the item, avoid asking questions that do not directly negotiate price or provide leverage for a discount.
When the seller offers to allow testing and examination of the product, avoid solely focusing on verifying functionality and quality as it may not directly impact pricing leverage in the negotiation.

When the seller has already stated the asking price and you want to negotiate a better deal, consider making a slightly lower offer than your target price to allow room for the seller to counteroffer and reach a mutually beneficial agreement.

When the seller shows willingness to negotiate and provides reasoning for the product's value, you should express concerns and propose a lower price while highlighting benefits for the seller to increase your bargaining power.
When the seller has already offered a discounted price, avoid introducing new conditional requirements that could weaken your bargaining position.
When the seller emphasizes the product's quality without addressing price concessions, avoid shifting the conversation towards product features instead of negotiating price terms.
When the seller counters with a higher price than their initial offer, avoid weakening your negotiating position by offering a lower price without leveraging potential trade-in options.
When the buyer offers a slightly higher cash amount along with a specific item from their trade list, it can strengthen their leverage and lead to a favorable agreement in price negotiation.

When the seller shows willingness to negotiate and mentions constraints on lowering the price, you should leverage comparative arguments like performance differences to justify a reduced offer and secure a better deal.

When the seller indicates a willingness to negotiate but mentions constraints on lowering the price, avoid suggesting a significantly lower offer based solely on wattage comparison, as it may jeopardize the negotiation process.

When the seller has already offered a price reduction from their initial ask, avoid making significantly lower counteroffers as it may weaken your negotiating position and lead to less favorable responses.
When the seller has previously offered a price of $40 and the buyer suggests a lower price, like $35, the buyer should confidently propose the reduced amount to secure a better final price.
When the seller emphasizes the item's quality and power, avoid making significant price reductions that undervalue the item and weaken your negotiation leverage.
When the seller offers a price reduction and delivery service, avoid increasing the offer significantly without gaining additional concessions, as it may weaken your negotiation leverage.

When the seller has already reduced the price to 400 and agreed to deliver the item, avoid accepting the offer without further negotiation to prevent weakening your position and securing a less favorable deal.
When the seller introduces additional items for extra cost, avoid asking about perks that may lead to upselling and distract from negotiating the main item's price downward.

When the seller maintains a firm stance on the original price, avoid removing potential bargaining chips by explicitly stating disinterest in bundled items, as it may limit opportunities for price negotiation.
When the buyer introduces lower market prices from other websites, you should acknowledge potential flexibility in pricing to open up negotiation space and improve buyer's leverage.

When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by offering a price slightly higher than the buyer's initial offer, you should hold firm to your target price to maintain leverage and potentially secure a lower final price.

When the buyer agrees to a higher price than their initial target, avoid immediately confirming the deal at that price, as it weakens the buyer's leverage and reduces the possibility of negotiating a lower price.
When the seller shows flexibility by offering a slightly higher price than the buyer's initial offer, you should accept the counteroffer to finalize a deal at a more favorable price point.
When the seller provides detailed information about the item's condition including minor flaws, you should ask targeted questions to uncover leverage for negotiating a better price.
When the seller confirms the product works perfectly and maintains the original price, avoid asking only about product functionality without linking it to negotiating a lower price.

When the seller justifies their price by highlighting product condition and includes a counteroffer with conditions, you should leverage specific product flaws to justify a lower counteroffer and move the negotiation closer to your target price.
When the seller sets a firm minimum price and hints at competing offers, avoid showing eagerness to close quickly as it can reduce your leverage and lead to higher prices.

When the seller emphasizes added value through bundled services, avoid proposing price reductions by removing those services, as it can strengthen the seller's leverage and increase the overall price.
When the seller offers a counterprice higher than your initial target, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting further negotiation to secure a better deal.
When the seller has made a reasonable concession and the buyer has accepted the offer, avoid making only polite closing statements that do not seek further negotiation or leverage.
When the seller confirms the item is in good condition and is selling only due to upgrading, avoid asking questions that do not create price pressure or lead to concessions.
When the seller responds to a low offer by adding value and raising the price, avoid making initial offers significantly below your stated target price as it weakens your negotiation leverage.

When the seller sets a firm minimum price but offers extras and delivery options, you should propose a slightly lower price combined with compensations like covering delivery costs to create flexibility and maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller counters with a price close to your initial offer and adds non-price benefits, avoid lowering your offer below your original target without gaining a clear price advantage.
When the seller has not responded to your initial low offer, avoid merely confirming your message without adding new negotiation points or concessions.
When the seller responds to your initial offer with a counteroffer above your price, you should start with a low offer to create leverage and encourage the seller to lower their price.
When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer above your initial offer, you should accept it to secure the deal and avoid prolonging negotiations unnecessarily.
When the seller emphasizes the item's high retail value and excellent condition without adjusting the price, avoid focusing solely on product details that do not advance price negotiation.
When the seller clearly states a firm lowest price, avoid confirming that price without attempting to negotiate lower or introduce additional leverage.
When the seller has stated their lowest acceptable price clearly, avoid immediately accepting without attempting to negotiate for additional value or a better deal.
When the seller sets a firm minimum price above your offer, avoid increasing your counteroffer too close to the seller's price as it reduces your negotiation leverage.
When the seller firmly states a lowest acceptable price, avoid quickly increasing your offer as it signals weakened leverage and reduces your ability to negotiate a better deal.
When the seller maintains a firm price but highlights product features, you should make a clear, lower counteroffer that acknowledges product specifics to encourage a price concession.
When the seller reaffirms the product's superior quality without adjusting the price, avoid shifting focus to product condition instead of pressing for price concessions.
When the seller makes a clear counteroffer with a specific price, you should accept or make a final offer close to that price to facilitate agreement and close the deal efficiently.
When the buyer reveals financial constraints and urgency, avoid shifting the negotiation focus to payment methods instead of addressing price reduction opportunities.
When the seller states a firm initial price, you should directly propose your maximum affordable offer to potentially secure agreement without prolonged negotiation.
When the seller clarifies the item's condition and sets a firm but negotiable price, avoid making an initial offer that is too low and questions product descriptions, as it may reduce your leverage.
When the seller maintains a firm price but introduces additional items to justify it, avoid focusing solely on missing components without leveraging this to negotiate a lower overall price.
When the seller maintains a firm price and declines to offer additional services, avoid shifting the negotiation focus to unrelated service questions that do not influence the price.
When the seller has stated a firm price but the buyer is uncertain about the item’s value, you should directly ask if the seller is willing to lower the price to prompt a potential concession.
When the seller has already lowered the price and included free delivery, avoid accepting the offer without further negotiating price reductions or additional monetary concessions.
When the seller has made a price concession and provided additional value or information, avoid simply acknowledging without advancing the negotiation or proposing further terms.
When the seller shows openness to trade offers, you should propose a trade item that can reduce your cash payment and invite the seller to evaluate its condition.
When the seller affirms the product's suitability without discussing price or concessions, avoid focusing solely on product features without linking them to price negotiation.

When the seller confirms the item is new and sealed but does not provide additional value details or price adjustments, avoid asking questions that do not create leverage or pressure for a better price.
When the seller firmly rejects a lowball offer without countering, avoid presenting your lowest price too early as it can reduce your negotiation leverage and stall progress.
When the seller maintains a firm price but offers non-price concessions, avoid focusing solely on price reductions without considering alternative value-added benefits.
When the seller maintains the original price but offers small additional perks, avoid shifting focus away from negotiating the core price reduction.

When the seller offers a small concession to sweeten the deal, avoid immediately increasing your price offer as it can weaken your bargaining position and encourage the seller to raise their counteroffer.
When the seller has made a counteroffer close to your target price, you should propose meeting halfway to encourage agreement on a more favorable price.
When the seller makes a clear final counteroffer that meets you halfway between your offer and their initial price, you should accept it to secure a better deal without risking losing the agreement.
When the seller firmly restates their asking price without engagement, avoid making a significantly lower offer that undermines your initial position and weakens your negotiation leverage.
When the seller justifies a price reduction by acknowledging product flaws, you should increase your offer to encourage further concessions.
When the seller has already disclosed an item's defect and justified the price, avoid asking redundant questions that do not introduce new leverage or directly propose a counteroffer.
When the seller lowers their price but still maintains a minimum threshold, you should make a significantly lower offer to test their bottom line and push for a better deal.
When the seller states a firm minimum price, you should make a slightly higher offer combined with a concrete concession like immediate pickup to successfully close the deal below that minimum.
When the seller has accepted your price offer and finalized the deal, avoid introducing new price negotiations or demands as it does not improve your position.

When the seller firmly rejects a low offer but emphasizes the item's value and extras, you should directly ask for their minimum acceptable price to uncover negotiation room and improve your bargaining position.

When the seller firmly rejects low offers and maintains a high minimum price, avoid conceding incrementally without eliciting reciprocal movement from the seller, as it weakens your negotiation leverage.
When the seller firmly rejects low offers and maintains a high price without concessions, avoid ending negotiations without proposing new offers or alternative terms to keep the dialogue open.
When the seller implies the item may have some wear, you should leverage this to justify your initial lower offer and propose cost-saving measures like self-pickup to encourage acceptance.
When the seller confirms standard included accessories without offering new concessions, avoid asking questions that do not create leverage for negotiating a lower price.
When the seller clearly states firmness on the initial price without offering concessions, avoid vague inquiries about price flexibility that do not apply pressure or advance the negotiation.

When the seller states a firm price but shows willingness to accept a lower price with specific conditions, you should present a concrete offer with added incentives like immediate payment or pickup to secure agreement.
When the seller offers a conditional lower price tied to immediate payment and pickup, you should agree explicitly and commit to those terms to secure the best possible deal.
